title: The Xero Remote MCP (Model Context Protocol) now generally available
snippet:
Today that changes. **Remote MCP is now generally available.** It’s the same Xero MCP server, hosted and maintained by Xero. Add the URL and sign in. That’s the setup.

is: **Model Context Protocol is a standard way for AI assistants to use tools.** An MCP server is a menu of things an AI can do, with clear instructions for each one. Point an AI assistant at the Xero MCP server and it can list invoices, create contacts or run a profit and loss report, because we’ve described exactly how.

Remote MCP launches with 39 tools, the catalogue the closed beta ran on, covering four groups of jobs:
- **Invoicing basics:** invoices, bank transactions, contacts, manual journals, accounts, tax rates and organisation details
- **Full accounting:** credit notes, quotes, items and tracking categories
- **Reporting:** profit and loss, balance sheet, trial balance, and aged receivables and payables
- **Payments:** creating and listing payments
The difference is where the server runs, and that changes who it’s for.
**Local MCP** runs on your own machine, which means it’s yours to look after. You install it, configure it, keep it running and update it every time a new version ships. If you want someone else to use it, they have to set it up on their machine too. It’s the classic trade-off of running software yourself instead of in the cloud: you take on the maintenance, and nothing works unless your machine is on.
**Remote MCP** is hosted by Xero. There’s nothing to install or maintain, you’re on the current version without updating anything, and because it’s a URL rather than a program on your laptop, you can build MCP clients that several people use, across more than one Xero organisation. It suits anything you want to share, run across organisations or not look after yourself.
There’s also a difference in where you can use it. The usual way to set up the local server is with a Custom Connection, and Custom Connections are currently only available in the US, UK, Australia and New Zealand.

Remote MCP is Xero’s official, supported server. It uses Xero’s standard OAuth 2.0 sign-in with PKCE, so users consent to which organisation an AI tool can see, and calls go through the same permissions and rate limits as the rest of the Xero API. The server itself runs on Xero’s infrastructure, so the piece sitting between your AI tool and your accounting data is one Xero builds, monitors and maintains.

title: GitHub - XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server: An MCP server that integrates with the MCP protocol. https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction
snippet:
# Xero MCP Server
This is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server implementation for Xero. It provides a bridge between the MCP protocol and Xero's API, allowing for standardized access to Xero's accounting and business features.
## Features
- Xero OAuth2 authentication with custom connections
- Contact management
- Chart of Accounts management
- Invoice creation and management
- MCP protocol compliance

If you don't already have a Xero account and organisation already, can create one by signing up [here](https://www.xero.com/au/signup/) using the free trial.
We recommend using a Demo Company to start with because it comes with some pre-loaded sample data. Once you are logged in, switch to it by using the top left-hand dropdown and selecting "Demo Company". You can reset the data on a Demo Company, or change the country, at any time by using the top left-hand dropdown and navigating to [My Xero](https://my.xero.com).
NOTE: To use Payroll-specific queries, the region should be either NZ or UK.
### Authentication
There are 2 modes of authentication supported in the Xero MCP server:
#### 1. Custom Connections
This is a better choice for testing and development which allows you to specify client id and secrets for a specific organisation. It is also the recommended approach if you are integrating this into 3rd party MCP clients such as Claude Desktop.
##### Configuring your Xero Developer account
Set up a Custom Connection following these instructions: [https://developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/custom-connections/](https://developer.xero.com/documentation/guides/oauth2/custom-connections/)
##### Required Scopes
Custom connections require different scopes depending on when they were created. **All scopes in the relevant list must be added to your custom connection:**
| Custom Connection Created | Required Scopes |
|---|---|
| Before Apr 29, 2026 | [SCOPES_V1](/XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server/blob/main/src/clients/xero-client.ts#L82-L90) (bundled permissions) |
| From Apr 29, 2026 | [SCOPES_V2](/XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server/blob/main/src/clients/xero-client.ts#L93-L112) (granular permissions) |
> **Note:** The MCP server automatically tries V1 scopes first and falls back to V2 if needed.

## For Developers
### Installation
```
# Using npm
npm install
# Using pnpm
pnpm install
```
### Run a build
```
# Using npm
npm run build
# Using pnpm
pnpm build
```

title: MCP server, connector and scopes (Oct 2026)
snippet:
Yes, two. Xero has a read-only hosted MCP server at mcp.xero.com behind its Claude connector (20 tools) and an open-source local server (51 tools) that reads and writes.
## Which route?
Use the Claude connector if you want questions and reports answered. It is read-only, has 20 tools, needs no developer setup, and Xero says it is free to add. On Claude Team or Enterprise, an Owner adds it first.
Use the local server only if an agent must create or change records (draft invoices, contacts, journals). It needs a Custom Connection (US$5 a month ex tax, AU, NZ, UK and US orgs only), Node.js 18+, and a client secret stored in your client config.
Before you turn it on: bank transactions and payments post at once, and journals can be posted. Set write tools to ask-every-time in the client, because the server has no approval step.
